safetyNote: Do not eat Echinoderma asperum. Poison-centre cases document an unpleasant alcohol-triggered reaction after its consumption. The German mycological society places it in the acetaldehyde syndrome group but states that its responsible substance is not coprine and remains unidentified. Contact a poison centre after a suspected meal, especially if alcohol was also consumed.

sections.title: Identification
sections.text: A robust lepiotoid mushroom with a pale tan cap densely covered by erect, dark reddish-brown pyramidal scales; the centre is darkest. The cap can reach roughly 10 cm or more. Its white to cream gills are free and crowded, with some forks possible. A pale stem bears small brown scales below a broad white to cream cottony or membranous ring, sometimes flecked brown on its edge. There is no basal volva.

sections.title: Habitat and season
sections.text: A saprobic mushroom found on soil, leaf litter and wood-chip mulch in woodland, parkland or gardens. In temperate Europe it is seen mainly from late summer into autumn. Odour descriptions vary, including rubbery or earthy comparisons, so smell alone is not diagnostic.

sections.title: Similar species and taxonomy
sections.text: Its brown pointed scales and white gills can invite confusion with other Echinoderma and Lepiota species or with parasol mushrooms such as Macrolepiota procera; the latter lacks this dense coat of sharp pyramidal scales. A 2025 molecular study found that the traditional broad concept of E. asperum contains at least four genetic lineages, so field characters cannot resolve every taxonomic boundary.

sections.title: Alcohol reaction
sections.text: A 2011 Munich poison-centre series reported three events affecting five people after mushrooms identified as Lepiota aspera, a former name for Echinoderma asperum. Symptoms resembled a coprine-like alcohol reaction. The DGfM says the inhibitor of acetaldehyde metabolism in this species is still unknown and explicitly distinguishes it from coprine. This is a reason to avoid the mushroom, not merely to omit alcohol at a meal.

sections.title: About the plate
sections.text: The plate shows an intact fruit body, a longitudinal section, the densely spiny cap from above and crowded white gills from below. The broad ring and scaled lower stem are visible. No spores are enlarged or detached in the illustration.
